title_en: Withdrawn 2026 members' bill for individual inhabitant-tax relief: policy proposal and legislative outcome

quick_take.what_changed: The House members' individual inhabitant-tax relief bill (221st Diet, House Bill No. 31) was withdrawn following approval by the House Committee on Internal Affairs and Communications on 22 October 2026. The proposed tax deductions never became law.
quick_take.who_is_affected: No immediate change follows for taxpayers, employers or municipalities. The withdrawn proposals remain relevant only to policy debate or any future separate legislation.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: Continue applying the current Local Tax Act. Do not use the proposed 1,780,000 yen combined deduction benchmark or under-16 dependent deduction as enacted tax rules.

paragraphs: The bill's sponsors argued that living costs and nominal wage growth had exposed weaknesses in individual inhabitant-tax deductions and incentives to work longer hours. These were policy assertions advanced to support a proposed framework, not findings that existing assessments were unlawful. The House subsequently withdrew the bill in October 2026, so none of its proposed measures became binding law.

As originally submitted, the bill called for an increase in the maximum basic deduction so that it and the minimum employment-income deduction would total 1,780,000 yen for the inhabitant-tax income levy from fiscal 2027. The proposed benchmark referred to average regional minimum-wage changes since fiscal 1995. The measure was never enacted; this is neither a present inhabitant-tax threshold nor a general income-tax or social-insurance exemption.

It also contemplated adding dependants younger than 16 to the inhabitant-tax dependent deduction from fiscal 2028, examining exemptions for specified vulnerable groups, and central-government measures to compensate municipalities for lost local revenue. These were conditional policy proposals in a withdrawn bill; they create no present entitlement, tax liability change or municipal reimbursement duty.

Four House members introduced House Bill No. 31 in the 221st Diet on 15 July 2026, and it was referred to the Committee on Internal Affairs and Communications on 23 July 2026. An older bill-progress page still shows consideration during recess, but that is superseded by the 222nd Diet's subsequent withdrawal record.

At its 22 October 2026 meeting in the 222nd Diet, the House committee unanimously consented to the sponsors' request to withdraw House Bill No. 31. The House's 222nd Diet bill list records its status as withdrawn. No enactment or promulgation occurred, and the proposed fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 tax changes were not implemented through this bill.

The withdrawn proposal had contemplated a framework directing the government to pursue subsequent amendments, including reconsideration of personal deductions by the end of 2028. Withdrawal terminated that proposal's legislative path; any revival would require another legislative initiative and enactment of appropriate tax-law amendments. No such revival is established by the cited sources.

confirmed.text: The House Committee on Internal Affairs and Communications agreed to withdraw the bill; the 222nd Diet bill list records the outcome as withdrawn.

expected: A new bill and separate implementing tax amendments would be required before any similar deduction policy could acquire legal force. The withdrawn bill itself has no pending legislative steps.
uncertainties: Whether the sponsors or government will introduce a materially similar proposal in the future, and on what terms, is not established by the cited official sources.
Any future deduction amounts, fiscal-year application, eligibility conditions or municipal compensation mechanism would depend on new legislation and cannot be inferred from this withdrawn bill.

paragraphs: The withdrawal leaves current individual inhabitant-tax assessment and special collection arrangements unchanged. Employers should not change payroll communications or calculations based on the former 1,780,000 yen combined-deduction proposal. Income tax and social-insurance contributions have their own legal bases.

Municipalities have no revenue-compensation claim under this withdrawn proposal. For planning purposes, payroll providers and local-government staff may monitor new initiatives, but the fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 figures in the old bill should be labelled historical and non-binding.
checklist: Keep current inhabitant-tax withholding and special-collection procedures in force; do not apply the withdrawn proposal.
Label any modelling of the 1,780,000 yen benchmark or under-16 dependent deduction as a historical, unenacted scenario.
Monitor newly introduced bills and enacted Local Tax Act amendments before changing employee advice or municipal revenue forecasts.
